annotations.title: package.json check: missing fields, vague ranges, no test script

description: Check a package.json for missing name or version, non-semver versions, vague dependency ranges such as '*' or 'latest', and a missing test script, with the offending dependency named. Choose this before publishing or committing a Node package manifest, to find missing name or version, a non-semver version, vague ranges such as '*' or 'latest', and a missing test script. Do not choose this for a vulnerability audit, which needs the npm registry, or for resolving version ranges. Example requests: Check this npm package manifest for problems before I publish. | Which of my npm dependency ranges are too vague? | Does this package.json have everything npm needs?

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

content.description: The customer's package.json, as text. Supported: JSON. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

inputs.title: package.json check: missing fields, vague ranges, no test script

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_package_manifest_check

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.
